newsitem.title: UK: Fresh snow clogs Europe, but temperatures ease.
newsitem.headline: Fresh snow clogs Europe, but temperatures ease.

text.p: Fresh snowfalls blanketed parts of Europe on Sunday, prolonging travel chaos and a deadly freeze, although elsewhere a thaw set in, bringing with it the threat of flooding as the grip of arctic weather eased.
Southern France was the worst hit, with authorities urging holiday-makers to delay their journey home after bad weather closed several motorways and virtually sealed off ski resorts.
Several hundred travellers spent Saturday night in schools and town halls after the A20 motorway in the Limousin region was closed. Traffic restarted at dawn but only on one lane.
In the Rhone Valley near Lyon in central France, fresh snowfalls on Sunday seriously disrupted traffic on the A7 Autoroute du Soleil (Sun Motorway) towards Orange.
Further south, three Pyrenees ski resorts were completely sealed off by heavy snowfalls. Three other resorts organised convoys of some 100 vehicles each to allow some skiers to leave.
Rail traffic was also disrupted with thick ice on power cables blocking the Marseille to Paris line and slower diesel trains replacing electric locomotives on the Bordeaux route.
Fresh snow also hit Belgium where six have perished from cold. Up to 200 people have died across Europe as the worst bout of winter weather for 30 years swept across the continent.
The homeless, the elderly, and those with too much seasonal spirit inside them have been the main victims of temperatures that plunged to below minus 26 degrees Celsius (minus 15F).
The death toll from the bad weather in Britain rose to 14 with the discovery of a man's body in the snow in the southern English county of Kent. He disappeared following a night out with a friend.
British authorities have turned their attention to flood damage as a thaw raised temperatures across the nation.
Fire brigades were called out to help thousands of householders deal with burst pipes and flooded rooms.

Italy was bracing itself for more snow, cold and high winds on Sunday and Monday, the end of the Christmas holiday, but forecasters did not expect temperatures to plummet to the levels of recent days, when four people died in sub-zero conditions.
Snow fell in Sardinia, which had so far escaped the worst of the bad weather, and in the lagoon city of Venice, the high waters rose another 16 centimetres (six inches).
The northeastern region of Friuli-Venezia-Giulia was gearing up for another cold and windy spell with an exceptionally strong "bora", the chill wind that sweeps along the Adriatic coast.

The cold weather has brought joy to skiers and skaters, with the Netherlands on Saturday able to hold a 200km (125 mile) skating marathon, linking 11 mediaeval cities by canal, for only the 15th time this century and the first time in 11 years.

A 29-year-old sprout farmer won the event, that attracted 16,000 competitors. But race organisers said a 57-year-old man had died, probably as a result of a heart attack as he battled against the freezing wind.
